name: open-spatial-lab-avatar-runtime
source: vendor/avatar-evaluator-v1 copy (web/vendor/avatar-evaluator-v1/mannequin/web/avatar/*.mjs and the fitting/*.mjs they import), the runtime the Lab page ran before 1.0.0. Code is unchanged except import specifiers; the vendor folder stays in place.
surface_differences: RemoteAvatar is not exported: the vendor copy has no remote-avatar module. The agreed surface named it; 1.0.0 leaves it out.
SolverStack (fitting/solvers.mjs) is not in index.mjs but web/avatar/actionforge-avatar.mjs imports it by module path, as it did from the vendor copy.
fitting/rig.mjs and fitting/roles.mjs are one-line forwards to runtime/scene-core/public/process/rig/, found through import.meta.resolve("#scene-manager").

fitting/map-clips.mjs is a one-line forward to runtime/scene-core/public/process/clips/map-clips.mjs; fitting/holds.mjs is a one-line forward to runtime/scene-core/public/process/items/holds.mjs, and equipment.mjs imports runtime/scene-core/public/process/items/placement.mjs, all found through import.meta.resolve("#scene-manager"); the body records of adam, megan, elizabeth and sophie carry face.eye_y_m and measures.back_surface_z_m.

avatar-motion.mjs, fitting/solvers.mjs and fitting/vendor/avatar-ik.mjs are one-line forwards to runtime/scene-core/public/animation/drivers/humanoid/, and locomotion.mjs to runtime/scene-core/public/navigation/humanoid/locomotion.mjs, found through import.meta.resolve("#scene-manager"); the page no longer fetches fitting/vendor/avatar-ik.mjs (the engine solvers import their own copy).

imports.note: The host maps three and three/addons/ (browser import map or Node resolution). All other imports are relative inside this folder, except the forwards and equipment.mjs, which reach the engine's process/ folders (rig, clips, items, and through them mesh), animation/ and navigation/ through import.meta.resolve("#scene-manager").

files.change: forward to runtime/scene-core/public/animation/drivers/humanoid/avatar-motion.mjs, which imports canEquip, GROUPS and splitClip from process/items/placement.mjs and STANCE_FADE_S from the solvers beside it; behaviour unchanged

item placement moved to runtime/scene-core/public/process/items/placement.mjs and re-exported; face and back slots (Equipment.face, Equipment.back, wearing, resolveItem, faceFit, SLOTS, slotOf); loading, overlays and the Equipment class stay here
forward to runtime/scene-core/public/navigation/humanoid/locomotion.mjs (the same bytes); behaviour unchanged
forward to runtime/scene-core/public/process/items/holds.mjs; adds the face and back slots (WORN_SLOTS, wornSlot, backAnchor, backPlane, fitBack, fitFace); held, carried and head items unchanged
forward to runtime/scene-core/public/animation/drivers/humanoid/solvers.mjs, which imports process/rig/roles.mjs, process/rig/rig.mjs and process/items/holds.mjs; behaviour unchanged
forward to runtime/scene-core/public/animation/drivers/humanoid/vendor/avatar-ik.mjs (the same bytes), named and default exports; behaviour unchanged

data.note: The data the Lab page reads with this runtime, at the same URLs as before 1.0.0 (unchanged). Avatars: web/avatar-equipment-layer.js prepared paths; items: actionforge-avatar.mjs ITEMS_URL and assetBase.

three.range: r160 and 0.186.1 passed; versions between were not tested
tested: 0.160.0 (Lab vendored core runtime/scene-core/public/vendor/three/three.module.js; addons from code/node_modules/three 0.173.0 examples/jsm, which the Lab page serves)
three.check: Node import-and-run of index.mjs: load adam (web/assets/actionforge/characters/adam/adam.avatar.json), create an instance, SolverStack on its body, take shield and hat from the page's item library (vendor items.json, 7 production items), run Locomotion + AvatarMotion + solvers 30 steps forward at 1/30 s. Same output on both versions. Textures stubbed (1x1 image bitmap); rendering not tested.

limits: Lacks the newer hand-skin fitting (level-2 hollow and box contact). 1.0.1 does not have Level 2 skin fitting.

Feet check (SCRAP Avatars acceptance: no case worse than 1.0.0, and with solvers on no frame below -2.5 cm) passes; the deepest frame with solvers is -0.04 cm. Known cases that miss the raw 2.5 cm rule in both 1.0.0 and 1.0.1, none from the hips rule: the mannequin's own walk clip (-2.63 cm), Adam's raw jog (-3.44 cm), Elizabeth's walk floating 4 cm (raw and with solvers; a heels case).
next: 1.1.0 from the Avatars frozen package once that runtime is fit for live use.
changes_from_1.0.0: Feet rule (SCRAP Avatars 1.0.1 candidate, manifest SHA-256 9d93e1ac27c741170f976d38e9dea7c808ee855d4cfa964d37c10a2a1dc5c4a2): clip pack reference_hips_height_m 0.9015 -> 0.9167 (rest pelvis above the floor; binary chunk identical); adam, megan, elizabeth and sophie avatar.json hips fields regenerated with floor-based heights (floor offsets 0.07, -0.07, 0.28, 0.10 cm).
clip-library.mjs pelvisScaleOf comment states the floor-based rule. No code change.
speed_mps and left_touchdown_phase are unchanged. Acceleration, scaled by pelvis_position_scale in locomotion.mjs, changes by up to 5.9% (Elizabeth).
